comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Thanks a lot @elisabeth.keller!  I think it might actually work with planewave mode and be much faster.  But I didn't look at the results, just checked that it didn't seem to crash.  Would you be able to test this please?  Basically: mode='pw' and refrain from setting the eigensolver to 'cg'.  Which corresponds to this version of the initial computation script:  

```
from gpaw import GPAW

from ase.build import molecule

atoms = molecule('C6H6')
atoms.center(vacuum=3.5)

calc = GPAW(mode='pw', xc='PBE', txt='benzene.txt', nbands=18)
atoms.calc = calc
atoms.get_potential_energy()

calc = calc.fixed_density(
    txt='benzene-harris.txt',
    nbands=40,
    convergence={'bands': 35},
)
atoms.get_potential_energy()

calc.write('benzene.gpw', mode='all')
```

Would you be able to verify that it works like this and update this MR?

There's also another example (wannier_polyacetylene) which might likewise speed up using pw mode.

Thanks again!

comments.author: elisabeth.keller
comments.body: Thanks for the suggestion. I changed the mode to 'pw' here and in the part for wannier_polyacetylene, see e1299986f194c3aa0cdfd6d7f5c94d5ae7308cab, and it speeds up the computations while the results are still accurate.
